rationale: In the BSB, the angel's last clause about Ishmael at Genesis 16:12, 'he will live in hostility toward all his brothers,' comes back almost word for word as the last clause of Ishmael's genealogy at 25:18, 'And they lived in hostility toward all their brothers.' The promise of descendants 'too numerous to count' (16:10) is followed in the same book by 'twelve princes of their tribes' (25:16), with God's 'He will become the father of twelve rulers' (17:20) in between. In their notes on 16:12, the Cambridge Bible ('Cf. Genesis 25:18'), Matthew Poole ('See Genesis 25:18'), and Rashi ('cf. Genesis 25:18') all point to the later verse. One caution: the Hebrew phrase the BSB renders 'in hostility toward' is translated in three named ways in the Pulpit Commentary's survey ('to the east of'; 'everywhere before the eyes of'; 'independently of'), and Ellicott notes that 'to the east' does not fit as well at 25:18. So what this row tracks is a phrase that recurs, and the 'hostility' sense is a translation decision. The verbs differ in Hebrew as well. Held's printed Hebrew of 16:12 has yishkon ('he will dwell'). At 25:18 Ellicott notes that 'the Hebrew is, he fell —that is, his lot fell; he settled there' (the verb naphal). So the English near-identity of the two clauses is partly the BSB's own smoothing. Graded motif rather than promise_fulfillment because the recurrence can be checked, while calling it a fulfillment would decide what the oracle meant. Graded strong because the wording recurs closely and three named commentators link the two verses.
